FLYPSE / DOCUMENTATION

Emulate federated learning across the Cloud–Edge in Python.

Implement the entities of a federation, split the data across them, and choose the devices they run on. Entities run as remote services and exchange real messages, so the statistics of the data and the limits of the system both shape the learning.

Run your first federation → Installation

Your first run

  1. Install FLYPSE →
  2. Build your federation →
  3. Run and inspect the reports →

Runs on your machine through Ray: no cluster required.

WHAT YOU CONFIGURE

Start with three building blocks.

01 / FEDERATION

Entities and connections

Implement what each entity does at every step, then connect them as a star, a tree, a ring or any graph of your own.

Build a federation → 02 / DATA

Splits across entities

Give each entity its portion of a dataset, uniform or skewed by label or quantity, and split each portion into train and test parts.

Split the data → 03 / SYSTEM

Devices and placement

Run on one device, on a copy of the topology of the federation, or on any ECLYPSE infrastructure with the placement strategy you choose.

Choose where it runs →

SCENARIO IDEAS

What would you like to investigate?

Illustrative research questions, not preconfigured benchmarks or measured results. Each requires its own model, data and system assumptions.

LABEL SKEW

Clients see different classes

Split the data with a Dirichlet distribution. How much heterogeneity can an aggregation strategy tolerate before accuracy drops?

Vary
The concentration of the split and the number of entities.
Inspect
Evaluations per entity and round, on their own test parts.
Model data skew →
HIERARCHY

Aggregators near the edge

Group clients under edge aggregators. Does aggregating often at the edge make up for rarer global rounds?

Vary
The shape of the tree and how often groups report to the root.
Inspect
Loss per version of the model, across its version levels.
Follow the hierarchical example →
SLOW LINKS

Some clients fall behind

Degrade a link during the run. What does an aggregator with a deadline lose, and what does it save?

Vary
Link latency, its timing and the deadline of the aggregator.
Inspect
Rounds completed, participants and late updates.
Follow the stragglers example →
Looking for runnable examples? Browse the example guides →

AFTER A RUN

Read what the entities reported.
Change one assumption.

Entities push the values they need during a run, and each record keeps who reported it, from where and when. Keep the seed explicit when comparing runs.

Read and query results → 
self.report(round=round, loss=loss)  # in an entity

process.run(seconds=10)
records = process.reported
frame = process.report.service()

Reports stay whole, whatever the report format. ECLYPSE metrics are available in CSV, JSON or Parquet, with a pandas or Polars report backend.

CHOOSE WHERE IT RUNS

Check the logic first. Add a real topology when needed.

SINGLETON OR MIRROR

Start from the federation

Run every entity on one device to check its logic, or give each entity its own device on a copy of the topology of the federation. There is no infrastructure to write.

Use a built-in system →
ANY ECLYPSE INFRASTRUCTURE

Bring your own system

Use the ECLYPSE builders or your own graph of nodes and links, with update policies that change it during the run.

Configure the system →
